findings.title: NilTopicUser causes 500 error on unsubscribe
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil for users who have never visited the topic (e.g. someone who only received the notification email). The very next line `tu.notification_level > ...` then raises `NoMethodError` on nil, producing a 500 instead of either muting the topic or returning a clean 404. The action needs to handle the nil case (e.g. create a TopicUser with the desired level, or short-circuit to a page that tells the user they have no subscription on this topic).

findings.title: GET-based unsubscribe is CSRF-vulnerable; no per-user token
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is exposed only via GET (config/routes.rb lines 440–441) and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`, and the action mutates state (`tu.save!`). Unlike the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` route which uses a unique per-user key, this route authenticates only via the session cookie, so any third-party page or email can embed `` (or equivalent link) and, if the victim is logged in, silently mute them on arbitrary topics. At minimum, the action should require a one-time token (as the email-key route already does), or be POST-only with CSRF, to prevent drive-by topic muting.

findings.title: Direct tu.save! skips TopicUser.change (race + no broadcast)
findings.body: The action uses `TopicUser.find_by(...).save!` instead of `TopicUser.change(user_id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`. `TopicUser.change` is the established entry point that (a) does an atomic upsert, (b) sets `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id`, (c) broadcasts the change on MessageBus so other tabs/clients update, and (d) handles the `RecordNotUnique` race. Bypassing it means concurrent clicks can clobber each other, the notification reason metadata is never written, and live UIs do not refresh.

findings.title: No rescue from Discourse::InvalidAccess on private/restricted topics
findings.body: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` will raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for topics the user can no longer see (e.g. removed from a PM, category access revoked). Unlike `show` (lines 88–95) which rescues `InvalidAccess` and removes notifications, `unsubscribe` lets the exception bubble, producing a 500. Users in this state should either get a clean 403/404 or have the action bail out before mutating any state. As written, a 500 is also raised if a brand-new user without a TopicUser row hits the page (the nil-`tu` bug), so the rescue is doubly needed.

findings.title: Toggle semantics don't match UI copy
findings.body: When the user is currently `tracking` or `watching` (notification_level > regular), the action sets the level to `regular` (1) rather than `muted` (0), and the template copy shown after the redirect is "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." The user will in fact still receive regular notifications, contradicting the page they land on. Either drop straight to `muted` from any level, or change the copy and the I18n string to reflect that they are merely being downgraded.

findings.title: Typo in property name: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The controller defines `stopNotificiationsText` (double 'i') and the template `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` references the same misspelled name. It works only because both sides are consistent, but it will confuse anyone reading the code. Rename to `stopNotificationsText` (and update the template) to match the I18n key `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`.

findings.title: Wrong tense in unsubscribe confirmation
findings.body: The string `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` reads "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." but it is rendered after the controller has already performed the state change, so the tense is wrong. It should read "You have stopped receiving notifications..." (or similar) and should accurately reflect the resulting notification level (the controller can downgrade to `regular`, not always to `muted`).

findings.title: No tests for unsubscribe_url in rendered email body
findings.body: The PR adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the existing builder spec but never asserts that this URL appears in either the text body or the rendered html body. The new `unsubscribe_link` I18n string relies on `%{unsubscribe_url}` being substituted and PrettyText-cooked into an `<a>` tag — a regression there (e.g. forgetting to pass `unsubscribe_url` from another caller) would silently produce a broken `[click here]()` link in every notification email and would not be caught by the current spec.

findings.title: No controller tests for TopicsController#unsubscribe
findings.body: There are no specs covering the new `unsubscribe` action. At minimum the suite should cover: (1) nil `TopicUser` does not 500, (2) `tracking`/`watching` users get downgraded, (3) `regular` users get muted, (4) unauthorized topics (removed from PM) get a clean response rather than a 500, (5) MessageBus publish on `/topic/<id>` is emitted with `notification_level_change`. The state-changing logic and its edge cases are uncovered.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header still points to user preferences only
findings.body: The `List-Unsubscribe` header is hardcoded to `template_args[:user_preferences_url]` (line 107) even though `unsubscribe_url` is now available per-topic. Modern mail clients (Gmail, Apple Mail) honor `List-Unsubscribe: <url>` for one-click unsubscribe. Leaving it pointed at `/my/preferences` means users who want to silence a single topic have to click through two pages, undermining the purpose of this feature. The header should include (or prefer) the per-topic `unsubscribe_url` for notification emails.
